LESSON: SUBTRACTION (8

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.3: Subtraction (8
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Subtraction (8, part of Numbers in Grade 4 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you estimate the difference between givennumbers? 2. 2. How can you createpatterns involving subtraction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. subtract up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Subtraction (8 in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping in real-life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Subtraction (8 in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. estimate difference by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different contexts,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Subtraction (8 in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. create patterns involving subtraction from up to 10,000,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Subtraction (8 in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate application of subtraction of numbers in real-life situations.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Subtraction (8 in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. subtract up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping in real-life situations,

   Subtraction (8 helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping in real-life situations,

   Subtraction (8 helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. estimate difference by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different contexts,

   Subtraction (8 helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. create patterns involving subtraction from up to 10,000,

   Subtraction (8 helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. appreciate application of subtraction of numbers in real-life situations.

   Subtraction (8 helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to subtract numbers up to 4- digit numbers without regrouping using a place value apparatus prepared from locally available materials,

2. jointly work with peers to subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping using number cards or charts,

3. share tasks with peers to approximate and work out differences by rounding off the numbers to the nearest ten,

4. work with peers to generate patterns involving subtraction of numbers up to 10,000,

5. jointly work with peers 1. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to subtract numbers up to 4- digit numbers without regrouping using a place value apparatus prepared from locally available materials,
2. jointly work with peers to subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping using number cards or charts,
3. share tasks with peers to approximate and work out differences by rounding off the numbers to the nearest ten,
4. work with peers to generate patterns involving subtraction of numbers up to 10,000,
5. jointly work with peers 1. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Subtraction (8 together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: learner generates patterns involving subtraction of numbers from up to 10,000

• Digital literacy: learner, in pairs, plays games involving subtraction using digital devices.

Values:
Respect: learner patiently works with peers to subtract numbers up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping using

number cards.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: learner uses locally available materials to prepare place value apparatus for subtracting

numbers up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate reading and writing numbers up to 10,000 in symbols to preparing planting site and

planting costs in Agriculture.

Main points to remember:

1. subtract up to 4-digit numbers without regrouping in real-life situations,
2. subtract up to 4-digit numbers with regrouping in real-life situations,
3. estimate difference by rounding off numbers to the nearest ten in different contexts,
4. create patterns involving subtraction from up to 10,000,
5. appreciate application of subtraction of numbers in real-life situations.
